# rawsock — spec

## Maturity

**Grade:** 3 · S3 E3 A2 H1 P3 · limited by scope (core), evidence (oracle MIXED), performance (not measured) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** parity — libpcap 1.10.6 (Linux live capture, `pcap_compile` filter language, classic pcap + pcapng savefiles), with the named rejections under "What is deliberately not done" (surveyed 2026-11-03)

**Audit:** review 2026-10-04 · mutation 2026-10-04 (39/41, 2 eq) · src ?

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-11-03 (200,000-run budget per harness clean, RAWSOCK_FUZZ: eth, hwaddr, arp, filter, pcap, pcapng) · ct n/a — raw sockets (keyword review, 2026-10-07) · panic 2026-10-30 (sweep + blind review: filter compile stack overflow on long and/or chains (leaf cap + gen depth 512), run jump saturation, cmsg/pcap totality, ifname NUL; delta audit 32/36 + 4 eq)

**Performance:** ref 1.05× libpcap 1.10.6 · fastest ref (libpcap is also the fastest implementation measured; no Go or Rust candidate was measured, see Backlog) (measured 2026-11-03, `zig build bench-rawsock`, 5 rounds, wall time, worst row; rows 0.13–1.05×: `filter_run` 1.05× (our interpreter vs `pcap_offline_filter` on the same 8 programs over 2 000 frames), `compile` 0.74× (eight expressions, ours unoptimised vs `pcap_compile` optimize=0), `pcap_write` 0.53×, `pcapng_read` 0.22×, `pcap_read` 0.13× (libpcap through an in-memory `FILE`, ours over a slice); info, not in the verdict: `compile_opt` 0.11× vs `pcap_compile` optimize=1, for which ours has no optimiser. Live capture is a kernel tie and not a row: both sides end in the same `recv` on an AF_PACKET socket, and libpcap's `TPACKET_V3` ring has no counterpart here. Run-to-run spread up to 16 % on this shared host, so 1.05× is inside the noise of 1.0–1.1×)

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** yes

Design + threat notes for auditors. Usage: see ./README.md. Attribution/provenance: original work of
the zig-libs authors (MIT).

**Where we are ahead:** the only pure-Zig, libc-free AF_PACKET capture **and** inject path we found: in-kernel classic-BPF attach, promiscuous mode, kernel drop counters (`Socket.stats`), the 802.1Q tag recovered through `PACKET_AUXDATA` (`Frame.vlan_tci` — the kernel strips it before a tap sees the frame, so a naive capture loses it), a `sockaddr_ll` decoder, an ARP codec, and real-segment ARP/IPv4 goldens from a veth pair. **Where we are behind** (re-checked 2026-11-03): no `TPACKET_V3` ring / `recvmmsg` batching; no `vlan` primitive; the generated filter code is unoptimised (longer than libpcap's, never different in meaning); no host-name/service-name resolution; Linux only by design (→ "What is deliberately not done"). Built since the survey: `filter.compile`/`run` (2026-10-04; on 2026-11-03 IPv6 `host`/`net`, bare `host`/`net`, `portrange`, `less`/`greater`/`len`, `broadcast`/`multicast`, `proto[off:size] & mask RELOP n` offset expressions, `arp`/`rarp host`), `pcap` savefiles, `pcapng` reader and writer (2026-11-03), `Frame.timestamp_ns`, `Socket.joinFanout`.

## Design & invariants

- **Linux AF_PACKET capture + inject, no libpcap, no libc.** Open a `SOCK_RAW` capture socket for
  one EtherType (or every frame, `eth_p.all`), decode the kernel's `sockaddr_ll` into a typed
  `Frame`, attach an in-kernel classic-BPF filter, toggle promiscuous mode, and cook-inject frames
  on a named interface (a `SOCK_DGRAM` socket where the kernel builds the Ethernet header) or
  transmit a complete frame on the raw socket (`sendRaw`). Original work of the zig-libs authors
  (MIT), starting from a minimal receive-only ~25-LOC core (`openPacketCapture`/`ifNameOf`); the
  send path, `SO_ATTACH_FILTER` filtering, `PACKET_ADD_MEMBERSHIP` promiscuous mode, interface
  lookup by name/index (there is no listing), and the typed `Frame`/`LinkAddr`/`EthHeader` decode are new construction. Wire layout
  clean-room from `packet(7)`, Linux UAPI headers (`<linux/if_packet.h>`, `<linux/if_ether.h>`,
  `<linux/filter.h>`), IEEE 802.3/802.1AB, and ARP, with EtherStruct (BSD-2-Clause) consulted
  only as a header-field-order cross-check (no source copied). libpcap was not
  consulted.
- **Pure helpers need no socket/privilege:** `EthHeader.parse`/`.write`, `parseHwaddr`/
  `formatHwaddr` (MAC ⇄ `"aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff"`), `LinkAddr.fromSockaddr` (the `sockaddr_ll` decode
  `recv` uses), `bpf`/`etherTypeFilter` (classic-BPF program builder; wire-format `BpfInsn` is 8
  bytes, asserted), `arp.buildRequest`/`arp.parseReply` (addresses surface as `netaddr.Ip`).
- **Raw errno syscalls, no libc:** all socket/ioctl calls go through `std.os.linux` directly, a
  conscious ceiling shared with `icmp`/`netlink`. Kernel struct sizes (`sockaddr_ll`, `BpfInsn`) are
  asserted in tests against the documented ABI.
- **Concurrency:** reentrant — no shared state; one `Socket` per thread/loop.

## Filter compiler, savefiles, timestamps, fanout (2026-10-04)

**`filter.compile`.** Recursive descent over the language in `src/filter.zig`'s header (nesting
bounded at 64), an AST of single comparisons (`load [x+]off | #pktlen; [and #mask;] jeq|jset|jge|jgt #k`), and code
generation by true/false labels: `a and b` sends `a`'s false edge to the failure label and its true
edge to `b`; `or` mirrors it; `not` swaps the labels. Every jump is forward, so the program is a
DAG; a jump longer than 255 instructions or a program past `BPF_MAXINSNS` (4096) is
`error.FilterTooComplex`, never a truncated jump. The meaning of each primitive was read off
libpcap's own output (`tcpdump -d`, black box): IPv4 ports require fragment offset 0 and locate
the header with `ldxb 4*([14]&0xf)`; IPv6 transport protocols also match through a fragment
header (44) but IPv6 ports do not walk extension headers; `port` alone is tcp|udp|sctp; `icmp` is
IPv4 only. libpcap's "non-network bits set" refusal for `net` is mirrored.

**`filter.run`.** The kernel's classic-BPF semantics: an out-of-bounds load, a division by zero,
an opcode the kernel would refuse at attach time or running off the end returns 0 (drop); a scratch slot nothing stored to reads 0. One `switch` over the full opcode (2026-11-03; it was a class/size/mode decode plus a zeroed 64-byte scratch array, 2.2× libpcap's interpreter, now 1.05×). It terminates in at most `prog.len`
steps because every instruction advances and no jump goes backwards.

**`pcapng`.** (2026-11-03) Reader: Section Header (either byte order, several sections), Interface Description (`if_tsresol` decimal up to 10^-18 and binary up to 2^-62, `if_tsoffset`, up to `max_interfaces` = 32 per section), Enhanced and Simple Packet blocks; every other block type is skipped by its length. Every block length is checked (multiple of 4, framing, trailer equal, inside the input) before a slice is formed; an instant outside 64-bit nanoseconds is `BadTimestamp`, never wrapped. Writer: host byte order, one interface, `if_tsresol` 6 or 9, EPBs.

**`pcap`.** The writer emits host byte order (as libpcap does); the reader takes either order and
µs or ns magic, and refuses a record longer than `max(snaplen, 262144)` (a corrupt length, not a
frame) or one past the end of the input, before forming any slice. A µs file stores a ns time
truncated, as libpcap does.

**Timestamps.** Best-effort (no new `OpenError`; the module's own example switches on that set
exhaustively, and so may a consumer): `SO_TIMESTAMPNS_NEW` (64-bit `__kernel_timespec` on every arch), falling back to
`SO_TIMESTAMPNS_OLD` on an older 64-bit kernel; the cmsg parser shares the bounded walk of the
`PACKET_AUXDATA` one and rejects a negative time, a nanosecond field ≥ 10⁹ and a u64 overflow.

**Fanout.** One `setsockopt(PACKET_FANOUT, group | (mode | flags) << 16)`; the kernel enforces that
every member agrees on mode and flags, and a test proves the defrag flag reaches it.

## Threat model / out of scope

**Linux-only by design** — no BSD `/dev/bpf` path, no cross-platform abstraction attempted.
**Privilege-gated:** opening a capture/inject socket needs `CAP_NET_RAW`; without it `open` returns
a distinct `error.AccessDenied` rather than a generic failure (interface lookups like `ifaceByName`
are unprivileged and always available). This module is a **capability**, not a policy — it does not
itself restrict which interfaces/EtherTypes a caller may open; that access-control decision belongs
to the deployment (capability grant, network namespace, seccomp). The in-kernel BPF filter
(`setFilter`) reduces what userspace *sees*, it is not a security boundary against a co-resident
process with the same capability. Received frames are attacker-influenced wire data on a shared
L2 segment (spoofable source MAC, malformed lengths); the typed decode (`EthHeader.parse`,
`LinkAddr.fromSockaddr`, `arp.parseReply`) must reject malformed input without panicking — that
tolerant-parsing guarantee is the attack surface to audit, not the socket layer itself. The filter
compiler and the pcap reader take caller-supplied input; both are bounded (nesting depth, program
size, record lengths) and return typed errors. Out of scope: `PACKET_RX_RING`/`recvmmsg`
batching, `TPACKET_V3`, IPv6 Neighbor Discovery (only ARP is implemented), pcapng blocks other than packets and interface descriptions.

## Verification

Root-free tests (pure helpers, `sockaddr_ll` decode, BPF encoding, struct ABI sizes, fuzz-style
never-panic checks) always run; the socket tests need `CAP_NET_RAW` and `SkipZigTest`
without it. Under an unprivileged network namespace where root has the capability
(`unshare -rn zig build test-rawsock`) all tests pass, including open/filter/promisc and an
inject→capture loopback round-trip on `lo`. **2026-10-04:** the filter compiler is checked frame by frame against libpcap 1.10.6 (`tcpdump
-n -tt -r`) on a 20-frame corpus (ARP; IPv4 TCP/UDP/ICMP/SCTP incl. IP options, both fragment
kinds, a 60-byte IP header; IPv6 TCP/UDP/ICMPv6, a fragment header, next-header 1; a runt; a
frame cut after its IP header; an 802.1Q-tagged frame; an unknown EtherType) for 35 expressions;
`run` is checked on the same corpus with libpcap's own `tcpdump -dd` programs; the pcap codec
reproduces two `tcpdump -w` files byte for byte (µs and ns) and decodes them to the times
`tcpdump -tt -r` printed. Live (netns): `Options.timestamps` lands between send and receive on
CLOCK_REALTIME, a compiled filter attached at open passes only its frame (and the kernel's verdict
equals `run`'s), a fanout group splits round-robin and refuses a member with another mode or
without DEFRAG. Mutation 2026-10-04: 41 mutants, 35 killed, 4 killed by new tests, 2 equivalent
and removed as dead code. Also real-capture goldens: a genuine ARP who-has/
is-at exchange and Ethernet+IPv4 framing captured with `tcpdump` off a real layer-2 segment — a
veth pair with each end in its own throwaway network namespace (`lo` never does ARP, so it can't
anchor this; a real L2 segment is required) — anchoring real Ethernet framing and the ARP wire
layout independently of `buildRequest`/`parseReply` agreeing with themselves. Run:
`zig build test-rawsock` (add `-Doptimize=ReleaseFast` for the release check; `unshare -rn` prefix
for the full socket path).

**2026-11-03 additions.** The new filter primitives are checked on a 30-frame corpus (the 20 above plus ARP who-has, RARP, an IPv6 multicast UDP datagram, a SYN, a SYN-ACK, a 200-byte multicast UDP, an echo request and reply, an IPv6 TCP frame from another prefix, an MF fragment) for 100 expressions: each expression's verdict list is what `tcpdump -n -tt -r` printed (recipe `tools/gen_filter_oracle.py`, which reproduces the corpus and the list byte for byte). pcapng: files converted by Wireshark's `editcap -F pcapng` (black box) decode to the same frames and times as the classic files they came from, and this writer's files are read by `tcpdump -r` and `capinfos` as the same three packets (recipe `tools/gen_pcapng_fixtures.py`). `unshare -rn zig build interop-rawsock` now also asserts `ifaceByName`/`ifaceName`/`hwaddr`/`ipv4Addr`/`ipv4Netmask` against what `ip` configured. Fuzz: `filter.compile` (well-formed program; `E and E` and `E or E` equal `E`; `not (E)` never accepts what `E` accepts), `pcap.Reader` and `pcapng.Reader` (records inside the input, termination, writer round trip), each with a reach assertion. Targets: `-Dtarget=mips-linux-musl -Dcpu=mips32+soft_float -fqemu` (big-endian, ReleaseSafe: 70 pass, 26 skip, only the two BE seed-corpus failures listed in Backlog) and `arm-linux-musleabihf -fqemu` (75 pass, 23 skip, 0 fail).

## What is deliberately not done

- **`TPACKET_V3` / `PACKET_RX_RING` / `recvmmsg`:** a new receive API with its own ownership rules, and no consumer is throughput-bound (axp captures a handful of LLDP/CDP/DHCP/ARP frames in a 4 s window); not now. It is the one place libpcap is faster than `recv`.
- **`vlan` primitive:** on Linux the kernel strips the tag before the filter runs, libpcap uses `SKF_AD_VLAN_TAG*` ancillary loads, and a userspace `run` has no frame metadata for them; not now.
- **Host names, service names, `gateway`, `ip broadcast`/`multicast`** (need the resolver, /etc/ethers or the interface netmask): never in a pure compiler; the caller passes numbers.
- **A BPF optimiser:** the code is longer than libpcap's but never different in meaning (verified on 100 expressions); not now.
- **pcapng Name Resolution, Interface Statistics, Decryption Secrets and custom blocks:** skipped by length, not interpreted.
- **IPv6 Neighbor Discovery, BSD `/dev/bpf`:** unchanged from the survey (no consumer; the AF_PACKET ceiling).

## Backlog / deferred

- **2026-11-03 (P):** only libpcap was measured. A pure-Go (`gopacket/pcapgo`) or Rust (`pcap-file`) savefile reader may be faster than libpcap's stdio path; not downloaded or swept in this pass, so `fastest` is `ref` by default, not by finding. Needed for P1.
- **2026-11-03 (mutation):** the new filter primitives, pcapng and the rewritten `run` have no mutation run; the 100-expression oracle and the fuzz properties were not shown to catch a planted mutant.

- **2026-10-30 (no-panic sweep GS):** `pcap.writeRecord` does not know the file's snaplen, so a record longer than `max(snaplen, 262144)` is written but `pcap.Reader` then refuses it (`RecordTooLong`). Not a crash; the writer should take the header's `snaplen` (a signature change) or refuse such a record. Decide with the consumer (axp-core does not use `pcap`). Also: the filter compiler caps a filter at `max_insns` comparisons while parsing (`FilterTooComplex`), so `Syntax` errors after that point are reported as `FilterTooComplex`.
- **Big-endian: the two seed-corpus tests fail on s390x** (BE sweep 2026-10-18, same on Zig 0.16 and 0.17; re-run 2026-10-19 `-Dtarget=s390x-linux -fqemu -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe`): `corpus: the hwaddr seeds drive both shapes…` expected 7, found 0; `corpus: the ARP seeds…` expected 4, found 0. Test-only: the seeds are `std.testing.Smith` streams written on a little-endian host, so their length/choice words read differently on BE and no seed reaches the accepting arms. The parsers themselves are not involved. Fix: pin the counts per endianness, or encode the seeds through the Smith writer at comptime.
- **2026-10-04:** survey items (1) pcap savefiles — **done** inside this module (`rawsock.pcap`;
  a separate `pcapfile` module would need a root `build.zig` entry, and the codec is ~150 lines
  that every capture user wants next to the socket), (2) the expression compiler — **done for the
  subset** in `filter.zig`'s header, (3) per-frame timestamps — **done**, (4) `PACKET_FANOUT` —
  **done**; the `TPACKET_V3` ring stays deferred: a mmap'd ring is a new receive API (block
  iteration, ownership hand-back to the kernel) with its own lifetime rules, and no consumer is
  throughput-bound (axp captures a handful of LLDP/CDP/DHCP frames).
- **Filter language beyond the subset** — IPv6 addresses (four 32-bit compares each), `portrange`,
  `len`, byte-offset expressions (`ip[6:2] & 0x1fff = 0`), `vlan` (needs the `SKF_AD_VLAN_TAG*`
  ancillary loads on Linux, since the kernel strips the tag first), bare `host`/`net` (libpcap
  also matches ARP/RARP addresses there), and an optimiser. Each is additive; the differential
  corpus is the place to anchor them.

- **`PACKET_RX_RING`/`recvmmsg` batching** — mmap'd zero-copy RX for throughput; not built.
- **`TPACKET_V3` block-based capture** — not built.
- **IPv6 Neighbor Discovery helpers** — the ND counterpart to the ARP codec; only ARP exists today.
- **Remains Linux-only** — the documented AF_PACKET ceiling (no BSD `/dev/bpf`) is permanent, not a
  gap to close.

- **Survey ranking** *(survey 2026-09-30)* — what a libpcap user hits first: (1) **pcap savefile read/write** (`.pcap`, later pcapng) — tcpdump interchange, and the natural test-fixture format; pure codec, small-medium; a separate `pcapfile` module may fit better than growing this one (no sibling exists: `ls modules | rg pcap` empty); (2) **a tcpdump-expression → classic-BPF compiler** (`tcp port 80 and host x`) — otherwise every filter is hand-assembled; medium-large, but pure Zig; (3) **per-frame kernel timestamp** (`SO_TIMESTAMPNS`/`PACKET_TIMESTAMP` cmsg, same path as `PACKET_AUXDATA` already parsed in `recv`); small; (4) `TPACKET_V3` ring and `PACKET_FANOUT` (already listed above); medium. All fit §2 (Linux-only stays an accepted ceiling).

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle EXTERNAL** — every wire or interop format the module speaks has bytes or verdicts from a foreign implementation or the kernel (below); the self-written residue is named.

**What the tests actually contain.** the `golden: real capture` tests in src/root.zig freeze a real ARP exchange and a real Ethernet/IPv4/ICMP frame captured with tcpdump off a veth pair in an unprivileged netns -- loopback cannot do ARP at all, which is why the pre-existing hand-computed fixture had never met a real L2 segment; since 2026-10-06 `arp.buildRequest` is anchored by the Linux kernel ANSWERING it (`unshare -rn zig build interop-rawsock -- --capture`: this module's `open`/`sendRaw`/`recv` on a veth pair, the kernel owning the target; request and the kernel's reply frozen in `src/testdata/kernel_arp.zig`, replayed by the "kernel ARP" test). The socket wrappers meet the kernel as a foreign peer only when that program runs (by hand); in the lane they stay self (loopback inject + capture of their own frames), which is the residue: those tests prove the wrappers move bytes, not that a foreign peer agrees. Anchored from outside since 2026-11-03: the filter compiler (100 expressions' frame verdicts from `tcpdump -r`, `run` over libpcap's own `-dd` programs; `tools/gen_filter_oracle.py`), classic pcap (two `tcpdump -w` files byte for byte) and pcapng (Wireshark `editcap` output decoded, this writer's output read by `tcpdump`/`capinfos`; `tools/gen_pcapng_fixtures.py`), the kernel's own filter verdict equal to `run` (netns lane), and the interface lookups against `ip` (`interop-rawsock`, by hand). Hand-computed only: `parseHwaddr`/`formatHwaddr` text forms and the `EthHeader` field edge cases (the header itself is also read off real captured frames).

**How it got there.** The anchoring work landed. DONE a326e4a: real ARP + IPv4 frames off a veth pair (loopback cannot do ARP)
